topic_summary: Analysis of the sharp rise in 'gray divorce' (splits among those 50+) in the United States, which doubled between 1990 and 2010. The phenomenon is driven by longer life expectancies, changing marriage expectations emphasizing self-actualization, women's financial independence, and generational unwillingness to remain in 'empty shell marriages' lacking vitality or connection.

key_entities: Baby Boomer cohort (generation driving gray divorce rates; married young under different norms)
Empty shell marriages (relationships lacking connection/vitality but maintained for external reasons)
Women 50+ (primary initiators of gray divorce; financially independent unlike prior generations)
Marriage as self-actualization institution (contemporary expectation vs. prior breadwinner/homemaker model)
Menopause (biological/psychological transition sharpening awareness of relationship inequities)
Second/third marriages (higher divorce rates; 'divorce echo effect')
Dating apps for older adults (14% of 60s, 12% of 70+ use; perception of options post-divorce)
Financial consequences (41% income drop for women, 50% wealth drop for both genders)
key_tensions: Longevity vs. relationship durability (unprecedented 50-70 year partnerships vs. evolved pair-bonding timescales)
Self-actualization expectations vs. sunk costs (desire for meaningful third act vs. financial/social costs of divorce)
Gender asymmetry in outcomes (women initiate but face worse financial consequences; men re-partner more easily)
key_mechanisms: Empty shell tolerance threshold (societal shift from staying for kids/stigma to exiting for self-fulfillment)
Women's financial independence enabling exit (Boomer women's economic autonomy vs. prior generations' dependence)
Menopause as reassessment trigger (hormonal/psychological changes sharpening awareness of relationship inequities)
Divorce echo effect (prior divorce experience lowering barrier to subsequent divorce)
key_absences: Children's perspective on late-life parental divorce (adult children's experience/outcomes not addressed)
Cultural/ethnic variation in gray divorce rates (data appears US-aggregate; no breakdown by race/ethnicity/religion)

omegas.description: What are the psychological/relational outcomes for adult children of gray divorce? Source material focuses on divorcing parents; children's perspective is structurally absent despite potential for significant impact on family system.

Do gray divorce rates vary significantly by race, ethnicity, religion, or cultural tradition? Data appears US-aggregate; cultural/religious commitment systems may alter tolerance thresholds or financial autonomy dynamics.

Is gray divorce a Boomer-specific peak or a durable structural shift? Researchers predict Gen X/Millennials will avoid similar rates due to later marriage age, but longevity_mismatch mountain persists. Deferred axis boomer_cohort_specificity bounds this uncertainty.

Is menopause a distinct causal trigger or a correlate of midlife reassessment? Research shows divorce rate spike during menopause years, but mechanism (hormonal vs. life-stage) remains contested. Deferred axis menopause_reassessment_trigger.

Do women's worse post-divorce financial outcomes persist long-term or recover? Data shows 41% income drop and elevated food insecurity for 6+ years, but longitudinal recovery trajectories beyond that window are not addressed.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan) + gendered_outcome_asymmetry axis

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Multi-lens scan (demography, gender studies, evolutionary psychology, economics, sociology) produced diverse axis set. Dark matter probes surfaced adult children and cultural variation absences. Deferred axes documented with clear structural rationale.
